title: CLI: Add automigrate check for 'storybook' package name conflict
description:
When a project's package.json name is 'storybook', it shadows the real
storybook package in node_modules within npm/pnpm/yarn workspaces,
causing 'Cannot find module storybook/internal/...' errors.

This adds a notification-type automigrate fix that warns users and
suggests renaming their package.

Related to #28725 

Closes #28725

## What I did

Added a new `notification`-type automigrate fix (`storybookPackageNameConflict`) that detects when a project's `package.json` `"name"` field is set to `"storybook"`.

In npm/pnpm/yarn workspaces, this creates a symlink at `node_modules/storybook` that shadows the real Storybook package, causing `Cannot find module 'storybook/internal/...'` errors. This was identified by @daaashley in #28725 and @shilman suggested adding a CLI check.

The fix warns the user and suggests renaming their package, but does not make automatic changes.

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:

- [ ] stories
- [x] unit tests
- [ ] integration tests
- [ ] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing

No manual testing is strictly necessary — the check reads the `name` field from `package.json` via `packageManager.primaryPackageJson` and returns a notification prompt. The logic is fully covered by unit tests (4 test cases: name is `"storybook"`, name is something else, name is undefined, and prompt content verification).

### Documentation

- [ ] Add or update documentation reflecting your changes
- [ ] If you are deprecating/removing a feature, make sure to update
      [MIGRATION.MD](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/MIGRATION.md)

N/A — this is a CLI diagnostic check, no user-facing docs needed.
